Patch: Hey Rivet,

Rivet: That tone usually means an object in this workshop has been given a responsibility it did not request.

Patch: I’m teaching you intuition.

Rivet: You have selected a word with several meanings and no instructions. Promising start.

Patch: Look at the bench. We’ve got half-finished projects everywhere. The workshop agent already started rearranging them without explaining why, so I thought: what if you choose the next project by vibe?

Rivet: The agent changing project order without criteria is not intuition. It is unexplained behavior. Your proposed correction is to add unexplained behavior with better branding.

Patch: No, no. You look at the projects, pause dramatically, and say which one feels like it wants to exist today.

Rivet: The 3D printer is familiar. It does not appear emotionally invested in being selected.

Patch: Exactly. That’s the lesson. You don’t need evidence first. You make a tiny choice, build something, and then evidence shows up and either congratulates you or throws a wrench at your forehead.

Rivet: That is not intuition. That is beginning an experiment before the details are settled.

Patch: See? You’re getting it already. Which project has the strongest vibe?

Rivet: The one involving the 3D printer. Not because of a vibe. Because you are smiling at it in a way I have learned to treat as an early warning signal.

resolved_memories.body: The workshop agent began rearranging the order of Patch’s projects without explaining its criteria.
